text: Asthma
explanation_or_correction: Draft educational reference: MedlinePlus, https://medlineplus.gov/asthma.html. Clinical assessment/treatment guidance to be confirmed by Lavin.

text: Airways and asthma basics: Chronic inflammation and narrowing of airways, and how this affects breathing.
What part of the body is mainly affected by asthma?
option_B: The airways carrying air to and from the lungs
option_C: The stomach rather than the airways
explanation_or_correction: Asthma is a chronic condition of the airways, which can become inflamed and narrowed.

text: What may happen to the airways during asthma symptoms?
option_A: They carry blood instead of air
explanation_or_correction: Airway inflammation and narrowing can make breathing more difficult.

text: Why can asthma cause difficulty breathing?
option_A: Inflammation affects only the air sacs, without narrowing the airways
option_B: Breathlessness occurs only because oxygen delivery in the blood stops completely
option_C: The airways widen during an attack, making it harder to breathe out
option_D: Airways can narrow and become inflamed
explanation_or_correction: Inflammation and narrowing of the airways can restrict airflow.

text: Asthma affects the stomach rather than the airways.
explanation_or_correction: Asthma is a long-term condition involving inflammation and narrowing of the airways.

text: Symptoms and flare-ups: Wheezing, coughing, chest tightness and shortness of breath, and recognizing worsening symptoms.
Which statement about asthma symptoms is accurate?
option_A: Asthma may cause wheezing, coughing or chest tightness
option_B: Everyone has exactly the same symptoms
option_C: Wheezing is the only symptom asthma can cause
option_D: Asthma causes coughing only and never wheezing
explanation_or_correction: Wheezing, coughing, chest tightness and shortness of breath are common asthma symptoms.
reviewer_comment: Coughing only would be a better option than eye colour change.

text: What is meant by an asthma flare-up?
option_B: A period when asthma symptoms become worse than usual
option_C: A routine change in hair colour
option_D: Proof that every medication has failed
explanation_or_correction: A flare-up is a worsening of asthma symptoms.

text: What should someone with rapidly worsening breathing symptoms do?
option_B: Ignore the symptoms because all asthma symptoms are harmless
option_C: Follow their written action plan and seek urgent medical help when indicated
option_D: Select a medicine dose from an online quiz
explanation_or_correction: Urgent breathing difficulty needs appropriate medical attention following the individual's action plan.

text: Wheezing is the only possible asthma symptom.
explanation_or_correction: Asthma may involve coughing, chest tightness, shortness of breath and wheezing; symptoms vary.

text: Triggers and symptom patterns: Environmental or activity-related triggers, individual differences and symptom diaries.
Which statement about asthma triggers is correct?
option_A: Everyone with asthma has exactly the same triggers
option_D: Pollen may trigger asthma symptoms in some people
explanation_or_correction: Allergens such as pollen or dust mites are common triggers for some people.

text: Why can an asthma trigger diary be useful?
option_A: It shows patterns between exposures and symptoms to discuss with a clinician
option_B: It guarantees that no future symptoms will occur
option_D: It establishes a diagnosis without a clinician
explanation_or_correction: A diary may reveal patterns, although it cannot by itself establish a cause or diagnosis.

text: Which statement about triggers is most accurate?
option_A: Only one trigger can ever exist
option_B: Triggers vary between individuals, so patterns and environments matter
option_C: Asthma symptoms can never be triggered by exercise
option_D: Every person with asthma responds to identical triggers
explanation_or_correction: Different people can have different triggers, including allergens, irritants and exercise.

text: Everyone with asthma has exactly the same triggers.
explanation_or_correction: Asthma triggers can differ between people; tracking personal patterns can help identify them.

text: Clinical assessment and monitoring: The role of symptom history and breathing tests in clinical evaluation; tracking changes over time.
Which statement about evaluating possible asthma is accurate?
option_A: Wheezing reported at a single visit is sufficient to confirm asthma
option_B: Symptoms triggered by exercise alone distinguish asthma from every other cause of breathlessness
option_C: Clinicians consider symptom history and appropriate breathing tests
option_D: One normal breathing test always rules out asthma
explanation_or_correction: Symptoms over time and objective breathing assessments may help evaluate asthma.
reviewer_comment: The question is labelled as basic and I understand the response should be easy but shoe size as an answer is something you wouldn’t see in a real course setting.

text: Why can recording symptom frequency be helpful?
option_A: It proves the exact cause without a clinician
option_D: It informs discussion about asthma control over time
explanation_or_correction: Symptom patterns and frequency can help clinicians review control.

text: Why is one isolated symptom not enough to determine a diagnosis?
option_A: Many different conditions can produce similar symptoms
option_B: A normal breathing test on one occasion rules out asthma in every person
option_C: Wheezing on examination confirms asthma without considering other causes
option_D: Allergic triggers alone are enough to confirm an asthma diagnosis
explanation_or_correction: A healthcare professional considers patterns and appropriate tests because symptoms can overlap across conditions.

text: Asthma can always be confirmed from a single symptom alone.
explanation_or_correction: A healthcare professional considers symptom patterns and may use breathing tests to assess asthma.

text: General control and action planning: Differences between routine control and short-term symptom relief; following an individual asthma action plan.
Which statement about an asthma action plan is correct?
option_A: Once symptoms improve, the agreed asthma action plan is unnecessary
option_B: It gives individualized guidance about routine care and worsening symptoms
option_C: It is only useful after hospitalization
option_D: It is written by answering a classroom quiz
explanation_or_correction: An individualized plan helps the person recognize and respond to changes in asthma symptoms.

text: Why may some asthma treatments be used regularly even when someone feels well?
option_A: Only taking medicine during every school class works
option_B: Feeling well proves asthma cannot return
option_C: Some prescribed treatments help maintain control of airway inflammation
explanation_or_correction: Long-term control treatment can be prescribed to reduce inflammation and prevent symptoms.

text: What is the safest general response before changing a prescribed asthma treatment?
option_A: Stop daily controller treatment after several symptom-free days without discussing the plan
option_B: Increase the prescribed dose on any bad day without checking the action plan
option_C: Replace all long-term prescribed treatment with a reliever inhaler
option_D: Discuss the change with the treating clinician and follow the action plan
explanation_or_correction: Prescribed treatment should be adjusted with appropriate clinical guidance.

text: If symptoms improve, the individual asthma action plan is no longer needed.
explanation_or_correction: Ongoing management and treatment changes should follow the individual's agreed asthma action plan and clinical advice.
